A certain author's work is essentially a story set in the present day, with an alternative reality going back to World War 2 dealing with cryptography. Very true to reality, if created history. The man knows history, and math, and it shows. It follows a slightly fictional history of cryptography through different family members in different timelines, in different areas. Think of places like Bletchley Park, the South Pacific, other locations, and modern Bitcoin and civil rights issues. I greatly enjoyed it, and think I learned a lot along the way. Although I am sure someone will come in and explain how I am wrong, it is a few years since I read the book. Oh, and he can't end a story properly. But it's great up till then, and the endings are "okish" but not quite what you were hoping for. My favorites by him are a novel about a virtual reality crash, which was written before virtual reality and mapping services existed, a book about a young girl and technology, a fun read, a work that was shall we say, not his best, a book about survival that I loved, a series I couldn't get past due to specific characters, and a few more to tackle. Oh, and his non-fiction book about computer history is a good read if you are into computers. Good or bad, I have always learned stuff from him in an entertaining way.
